question.text: Which of the following features is UNIQUE to Mutual Funds and NOT available in PMS or AIFs?

answer.text: Daily NAV disclosure, mandatory TRI benchmarking, and standardized scheme categorization by SEBI

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A workbook (p40-p41 and p48-p50), mutual funds operate under SEBI's standardised scheme categorisation framework comprising 37 categories (including 11 equity sub-categories) with daily NAV disclosure for open-ended schemes and mandatory TRI benchmarking under the disclosure norms on p77-p78. Treated as a bundle, this transparency framework is what marks the MF regulatory regime out from PMS and from AIF (where p96-p98 allow NAV declaration daily, monthly or quarterly as specified in the placement memorandum, without an MF-style categorisation requirement). The Trap: Professional management (Option A) and SEBI regulation (Option B) are common to MF, PMS and AIF. Tax benefits (Option D) are not exclusively a mutual fund feature. The MF-specific element is the combined transparency bundle of daily NAV, mandatory TRI benchmarking and SEBI categorisation taken together. Note: The categorisation framework is currently 37 categories (not 36), and AIFs can declare NAV daily, monthly or quarterly as specified — so it is incorrect to say daily NAV is unavailable to AIFs.
